title: Recovering Mixtures of Two Causal Trees with Interventions on at Most Three Targets
banked_reason: D0.5 cold referee: achieved subfield with paper-score ceiling 6.7 below the field gate 7.4; proof panels passed, and no honest in-scope repair closes the gap.
gap_reasons: The delivered results establish exact-oracle directed-union recovery with interventions of size at most three, an observable instance-dependent experiment bound, complete size-two impossibility, and a sharp cubic nonadaptive requirement; they do not establish the full-class adaptive minimax frontier or a universal quadratic adaptive guarantee.

The package remains confined to population CI oracles and simultaneous intervention-mixture faithfulness, with no finite-sample testing theory, robustness analysis, component recovery, or concrete intervention-cost application.
Those restrictions and the limited econometric significance evidence hold the projected leading-journal score below the strongest field-tier examples despite the substantive graph-theoretic results.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery proved a graph-only three-target recovery theorem with an observable experiment bound, strengthened the hard construction to acyclic unions, and derived complete size-two indistinguishability plus exact deterministic and randomized nonadaptive lower bounds. Both proof-focused D0.5 panels passed without findings. The field-tier bid failed only at the calibrated significance gate: closing it would require a new full-class adaptive minimax result, finite-sample robustness theory, component recovery assumptions, or a substantial application rather than a repair to the completed mathematics.
tldr: For population mixtures of two distinct directed causal trees with fixed positive mixing weights, shared stochastic hard-intervention kernels, intervention-mixture faithfulness for every target set, and exact conditional-independence-oracle access, an executable SCC-batched algorithm recovers the directed edge union using targets of size at most three and at most \(n+\binom n2+(n-1)|E_{\mathrm{union}}|+A\) experiments. On acyclic directed unions, every residual cell has size at most one, so \(A=0\) and \(Q\le(5n^2-7n+4)/2\). Nevertheless, positive-rational binary witnesses whose two acyclic union graphs differ exactly by one edge force every deterministic nonadaptive exact design to query all \(\binom n3\) triples, while randomized nonadaptive error \(\varepsilon<1/2\) forces expected triple coverage at least \((1-2\varepsilon)\binom n3\). Complete transcripts also rule out worst-case success above \(1/2\) for arbitrary randomized adaptive learners restricted to size-at-most-two interventions. No universal quadratic adaptive guarantee, finite-sample CI procedure, component recovery, or optimal dependence on \(A\) is claimed.
gap: The closest interventional mixture paper separates a sharp local target-size theorem from a global \(O(n^2)\)-experiment algorithm whose targets can grow with cycle breaking and accumulated parents. It explicitly leaves constrained-size experiment-count lower bounds open. Existing observational mixture graphs, single-DAG separating systems, ordinary reachability queries, and rank-based mixture identification do not settle global size-three recovery or complete-CI transcript indistinguishability in this model.
fill: Prove the SCC induction and injective charging theorem, realize fixed graphical collisions by simultaneously faithful positive rational models with unchanged weights and shared intervention kernels, and use the componentwise sink-leaf-padded unique-triple family to show that nonadaptivity alone can force cubic cost even when every directed union graph has SCC size at most two.
